html:
The Syilx, or Okanagan people, are an Interior Salish nation of the Okanagan valley and the nearby Columbia plateau, in southern British Columbia and north central Washington. Syilx tmixʷ is their name for their homeland. They speak nsyilxcən.

They moved through the year between fishing camps on the rivers, root digging grounds and mountain hunting grounds, and spent the winter in pit houses dug into the ground. Salmon from the Okanagan and Columbia rivers was central, and the falls at Kettle Falls were a great gathering place.

In 1846 the Oregon Treaty split their land between British and American territory along the 49th parallel. On the US side many Syilx were placed on the Colville reservation; in Canada they form the bands of the Okanagan Nation Alliance. See also Okanagan.
